scope: Acquisition-domain evidence used to prevent cross-instrument and cross-CE pooling in the V15 feature-fragment benchmark.

sources.title: MassBank3 API OpenAPI 3.0 specification
supports: filtered record retrieval
individual record retrieval
repository release metadata
does_not_support: upgrading contributor free text CID to PSI beam-type CID
converting collision-energy units

sources.title: Q Exactive HF Software Manual, P/N 1372090 Revision A
supports: NCE is dimensionless
NCE is approximately the HCD energy in eV only for a reference ion at m/z 500 and charge 1
actual HCD energy is calculated from precursor mass and charge
multiple NCE values create one spectrum containing fragments from the steps
does_not_support: treating NCE as eV for arbitrary precursors
treating stepped NCE as a fixed-energy spectrum

sources.title: Q Exactive HF-X Software Manual, P/N BRE0012262 Revision A
supports: the instrument distinguishes normalized collision energy from absolute collision energy
charge changes the absolute energy needed for fragmentation
does_not_support: a universal conversion between Q Exactive models
a universal conversion from HCD settings to QTOF settings

sources.title: Agilent MassHunter Workstation TOF/Q-TOF Familiarization Guide
sources.locator: Auto MS/MS collision energy formula setup
supports: a method can compute collision energy from precursor m/z using a slope and offset
the guide's example coefficients are compound- and charge-dependent method settings
does_not_support: using the example slope and offset as a vendor-wide conversion
treating an m/z-dependent energy as a fixed-energy spectrum

sources.title: Comparison of in-source collision-induced dissociation and beam-type collision-induced dissociation of emerging synthetic drugs using a high-resolution quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometer
sources.locator: experimental comparison across fragmentor voltages and collision energies
supports: in-source CID and collision-cell beam-type CID are distinct acquisition conditions
fragment abundances depend on the applied energy setting
does_not_support: assigning beam-type CID when a repository record only says CID

sources.title: X500R QTOF System Compendium
sources.locator: example acquisition methods reporting CE 35 V and CES plus or minus 15 V
supports: SCIEX methods report collision energy in V
collision energy spread combines a range around a center value
does_not_support: treating a CES spectrum as fixed at its center value
converting V to MassBank eV literals

sources.title: TripleTOF 5600 System User Guide
sources.locator: Q2 collision cell and acquisition parameters
supports: fragmentation occurs in the Q2 collision cell
collision gas and collision energy are separate method parameters
does_not_support: inferring CES or dynamic CE when these fields are absent from a repository record

sources.title: Distinguishing N- and O-glycopeptides using collision-energy-resolved QTOF tandem mass spectrometry
sources.locator: Impact II collision-energy series from 10 to 140 eV
supports: fragment channels change across a wide collision-energy series
useful energy ranges depend on precursor m/z and structural channel
does_not_support: a universal Bruker energy conversion for small molecules
transferring glycopeptide-specific fragmentation thresholds to metabolite classes

sources.title: Bruker QTOF mass spectrometry overview
sources.locator: quadrupole isolation and controlled MS/MS fragmentation
supports: Bruker QTOF instruments use a quadrupolar system for isolation and controlled MS/MS fragmentation
does_not_support: the exact activation controlled vocabulary or collision-cell region of an individual MassBank record

sources.title: The Simultaneous Acquisition of Exact Mass Data Using Alternating Collision Cell Energy: MSE
sources.locator: Q-Tof Premier T-Wave collision cell and alternating low/high energy acquisition
supports: MSE alternates low- and high-collision-cell-energy functions
the high-energy function contains fragment ions without precursor selection
fixed and ramped high-energy methods are distinguishable acquisition conditions
does_not_support: treating MSE as precursor-selected MS/MS
assigning MSE when the repository record lacks an MSE label

sources.title: Tandem Mass Spectrometry across Platforms
sources.locator: comparison of Agilent, Bruker, SCIEX, Waters, and Thermo instruments across collision energies
supports: spectral similarity changes with collision energy and instrument platform
high cosine similarity can occur for different structures
fragment spectra alone do not establish exact identity or resolve isomers
does_not_support: a universal cross-vendor collision-energy conversion
using a cross-platform similarity result as standard confirmation

sources.title: Comparison of peptide fragmentation on Bruker Maxis II QTOF CID and Thermo Q Exactive Focus HCD
sources.locator: direct instrument comparison in the reported peptide experiment
supports: matched fragmentation extent required different instrument settings in the reported experiment
does_not_support: a model-independent conversion
a conversion validated for small-molecule chemical classes

families.activation_architecture: HCD with Orbitrap mass analysis; exact collision-cell metadata are preserved as reported or marked unreported
QTOF collision-cell CID is documented for the family; benchmark records retain the contributor literal CID and do not claim PSI beam-type CID
Q2 collision-cell CID is documented for the family; benchmark records retain contributor CID without a PSI beam-type-CID upgrade
Quadrupole-isolated QTOF MS/MS fragmentation is documented; benchmark records retain contributor CID without a PSI beam-type-CID upgrade
Q-Tof Premier collision-cell fragmentation is documented; benchmark records retain LOW-ENERGY CID and do not infer MSE or PSI beam-type CID

benchmark_conclusion.reason: Each CE series had 11 shared test identities; the preregistered minimum was 20.
